exampleAnswers.title: Identifying Elements of a Multiple Linear Regression

question.text:
$x_1$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$
$x_2$ $9$ $12$ $16$ $20$ $23$
$x_3$ $1$ $5$ $7$ $11$ $14$
$y$ $5$ $8$ $12$ $14$ $18$

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2+ \beta_3 x_3$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2\\ \beta_3\end{bmatrix} = (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
question.explanation:
$x_1$ $\color{blue}1$ $\color{blue}2$ $\color{blue}3$ $\color{blue}4$ $\color{blue}5$
$x_2$ $\color{purple}9$ $\color{purple}12$ $\color{purple}16$ $\color{purple}20$ $\color{purple}23$
$x_3$ $\color{green}1$ $\color{green}5$ $\color{green}7$ $\color{green}11$ $\color{green}14$
$y$ $\color{red}5$ $\color{red}8$ $\color{red}12$ $\color{red}14$ $\color{red}18$

The coefficients of the hyperplane

\[ y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_3 \]

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{purple}9& \color{green}1 \\ 1 & \color{blue}2 & \color{purple}12& \color{green}5 \\ 1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{purple}16& \color{green}7 \\ 1 & \color{blue}4 & \color{purple}20& \color{green}11 \\ 1 & \color{blue}5 & \color{purple}23& \color{green}14 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}5 \\ \color{red}8 \\ \color{red}12 \\ \color{red}14 \\ \color{red}18 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
